note: Every company in this file is fictional. `about` is written as a search snippet would read. The price floor is the point: the right sector at the wrong size is a bad fit.

profile.value_proposition: Independent ERP implementation for mid-sized manufacturers who have outgrown spreadsheets and Sage: shop floor to finance, live in nine months.

pages./: Foundry Lane Consulting. ERP for manufacturers who make real things. Speak to a manufacturing systems lead.
pages./services: We select, implement and rescue ERP systems for UK manufacturers with 100 to 1,000 employees and £15m to £200m turnover. We connect MRP, shop-floor data capture, quality and finance. 60 consultants in Birmingham and Sheffield, working on site across the UK.
pages./clients: Clients include Brindley Castings, Tame Valley Fasteners and Arden Food Machinery. Typical triggers: a failed audit, an acquisition, a new plant, a legacy system going out of support, or a finance director who can no longer close the month.
pages./engagements: Engagements start at £80,000 and a full implementation is typically £250,000 to £600,000. We are not the right firm for businesses under fifty staff, and we do not resell software.

ground_truth: UK manufacturers with roughly 100-1,000 employees (turnover about £15m-£200m) making physical products: castings, fasteners, machinery, food manufacturing, plastics, automotive components, electronics assembly. Strongest when a trigger is visible: acquisition, new site, rapid growth, legacy system end-of-life. The buyer is a finance, operations or IT director. Not ERP vendors, resellers or IT consultancies; not manufacturers under about 50 staff (cannot afford an £80k floor); not multinationals with a global ERP template; not non-manufacturers.
